speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what happens when you wake up frightened? Do you see anyone there, or do you feel like you are falling?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes happen specifically during the night while she is asleep, or do they occur when she wakes up naturally? Also, has anyone noticed your feet jerking or a sensation of falling right before you wake up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder.

Given the clear recall of bad dreams and the ability to be consoled immediately upon waking, this presentation is distinct from sleep terrors. I will not request further testing as the clinical picture is already sufficient for a diagnosis based on the DSM-5 criteria.
